property_summary: After Collect is called, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its value set during initialization.
After any call to Collect, the stored MinSum value equals the value it was initialized to.
The value of MinSum remains constant across calls to Collect after initialization.
After Collect is called, MinSum is always less than or equal to uint256 max.
The MinSum state variable remains unchanged after any call to Collect(uint256), regardless of the call's arguments.
After calling Collect(uint256), the value of MinSum remains unchanged.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the value returned by MinSum() is equal to the value set by the last successful SetMinSum call before initialization.

After a call to Collect(uint256), the value of MinSum is equal to the value returned by c.MinSum() before the call, and that value is either the initial 0 or the value set by a single successful SetMinSum call before Initialized().
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the value returned by MinSum() is exactly the value that was set by the last SetMinSum call (if any) that occurred before Initialized() was called.
A call to Collect(uint256) should never change the value of MinSum, regardless of other calls.
After a call to Collect with any amount, the Log address remains the zero address if SetLogFile was never called before initialization.
After any call to Collect that succeeds (does not revert), the LogFile address must equal the address set by SetLogFile, or be address(0) if SetLogFile was never called before initialization.
After any call to Collect that does not revert, the LogFile must have been set to a non-zero address via SetLogFile.
If SetLogFile was not called before initialization, the LogFile address remains address(0) after any Collect call.

After any call to Collect that succeeds (does not revert), the LogFile address must equal the address set by SetLogFile if SetLogFile was called before initialization, otherwise it must remain address(0).
After a Collect call, the LogFile address remains unchanged.
After a Collect call, SetLogFile() returns the address originally assigned via SetLogFile (non-zero), not the zero address.
After a Collect call, the value of SetLogFile() is not the zero address.
After any successful Collect call, the LogFile address stored in the contract before Collect is never changed by the Collect call.
After any Collect call, the SetLogFile() value equals the initially stored LogFile address.

After any sequence of calls followed by a Collect call that attempts to transfer value, the contract's SetLogFile address remains unchanged (it stays address(0) because SetLogFile never reverts in the reference and always reverts in the mutant).
After any sequence of calls to Put followed by a successful Collect that emits a Log, the Log.LogFile address is unchanged from the initial value.
After a Collect call, the SetLogFile getter returns the same address as the initial address set in setUp (address(0)).
After any call to Collect, the address returned by SetLogFile is either the zero address or the address of the LogFile that was set before Initialized.
After any call to Collect, the address returned by SetLogFile remains the same as before the call.
After any call to Collect, the SetLogFile state variable remains unset (address(0)) if the contract was never initialized with a log address.
LogFile address is always set after a Collect call if the contract was initialized with a log address.
After any Collect call that succeeds, the LogFile address remains unchanged from its initial value of address(0).
The LogFile address equals the address passed to SetLogFile if the contract was initialized by calling Initialized after SetLogFile.
After Collect, the log address is always equal to what was set by SetLogFile (if any), regardless of whether SetLogFile was called before Initialized.
After calling Collect with any parameters, the address of the LogFile contract stored in the Log state variable must equal the last address set by SetLogFile.
After Collect completes, the Log address equals the address set by the last call to SetLogFile.

After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the address stored in the Log state variable at the time of Collect's execution must equal the address set by the last successful call to SetLogFile, even if Initialized has been called.
After any call to Collect, the value stored in the Log state variable equals the last address passed to SetLogFile, even if Initialized was called.
After Collect completes, the LogFile address stored in the contract is the address set by the last successful SetLogFile call, regardless of Initialized being called.
Collect should successfully transfer funds only when the caller's balance is at least MinSum.
Collect should only decrease the caller's balance when the caller's balance is >= MinSum.
After calling Collect with msg.sender who has sufficient balance (>= MinSum), the balance of the caller should decrease when block.timestamp exceeds unlockTime.
After Collect is called with sufficient balance, the caller's account balance should remain non-negative.
Collect does not decrease the caller's balance when the caller's balance is less than MinSum.
The contract should not allow Collect to succeed when the requested amount is greater than the caller's balance.
If Collect succeeds (does not revert), the caller's balance should decrease by exactly the amount withdrawn.
The Collect function should only transfer funds when the requested amount is less than or equal to the caller's balance.

After Collect is called, if the caller's balance was at least MinSum and the timestamp is past the unlock time, then the caller's balance should have decreased by an amount equal to the amount passed to Collect (i.e., the new balance equals old balance minus _am).
Collect should only transfer tokens when the requested amount is less than or equal to the caller's balance.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance should decrease by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After a call to Collect, the condition block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime should hold if the withdrawal was allowed.
Collect function should only succeed when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime.
If a Collect call succeeds (does not revert), the caller's balance in Acc mapping should be decreased by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After any Collect call that does not revert, the caller's unlockTime in Acc must be strictly less than the current block timestamp.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the caller's balance in Acc does not exceed the amount they sent via Put plus the amount they collected.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance in Acc increases by exactly _am, not decreases.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance in Acc decreases by exactly _am, not increases.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance of Ether (address(this).balance) does not increase by more than _am.
After a successful Collect call, the total of the caller's Acc balance and ether balance remains constant (does not change).
After a Collect call, the sender's balance in the contract decreases by exactly _am.
After a call to Collect(uint256 _am), the amount of ether actually transferred to msg.sender equals the amount _am that was debited from the contract's record.
After a successful Collect call, the amount of ether sent to msg.sender equals the _am parameter.
After a Collect call that succeeds (does not revert), the caller's ETH balance increases by exactly _am.
After a successful Collect call, the contract's total balance (address(c).balance) decreases by the amount _am sent to the caller.
